impact: act1 writes DECISION.md and decision.json through two separate injected effects, and writeDecisionRecord additionally removes attempt-report.json. Each is wrapped in step(), so any failure is reported as a TransitionError and the gate exits 5 — but the artifacts left on disk can be inconsistent. If the record write fails after the document write, new prose sits beside an old machine verdict; if the attempt-report removal fails after the record is written, two mutually exclusive artifacts coexist even though act1 reported failure. Nothing is unrecoverable: a re-run regenerates all three from the same evidence, and the exit code says loudly that the run did not complete. The fix is the same shape as ISS-049 — stage the document, the record and the removal, then commit them as one unit through a single publish step rather than three independent ones — which is why it is filed alongside that issue rather than patched here. Both should be done together, since they are the same transaction boundary seen from two files.
title: T-009: the decision artifacts are written as separate effects, so a partial Act 1 leaves them disagreeing
